The one-key first-message Auth game (Lemma 1, second conjunct)

Trusted: the statement. Every definition in this file is part of the one-key first-message authentication and privacy statement SignalPqxdh.Security.PqxdhAuth1KeySecureδ (Security/Auth/Headline.lean), the second conjunct of PqxdhSecureδ in Lemma 1 (SignalPqxdh.Security.PqxdhCorrectAndSecureδ, Security/HeadlineDelta.lean). See Computational/docs/TRUSTED_BASE.md.

This file defines the mutual-authentication and first-message payload-privacy game (Auth), modeled after Fiedler–Günther (Eurocrypt 2025, Game 2) and Bhargavan–Jacomme–Kiefer–Schmidt (USENIX Security 2024), together with its key-schedule PRF and AEAD assumptions and closed-form advantage bound pqxdhAuthBound. In pqxdhAuthImpl1Key, .initPrin u samples a single Curve25519 identity scalar for both X25519 key agreement and XEdDSA signing (ikSignPk = ikAPk = P.x25519Base secIKA0, DEV-C5) and delegates all other queries to the shared two-key oracle body pqxdhAuthImpl true true (DEV-PQ13); Lemma 1 reads only the one-key advantage Auth1KeyAdvantage.

Key-schedule and AEAD assumptions

First-message AEAD (AeadIndCpa)

structure AeadIndCpaAdvL47–55 ↗#

Two-stage adversary against one-time left-or-right IND-CPA of the first-message AEAD: choose outputs (ad, m0, m1, st) and dist guesses the challenge bit from st and the challenge ciphertext.

structure AeadIndCpaAdv where State : Type := Bytes choose : OracleComp PrimBaseSpec (Bytes × Bytes × Bytes × State) dist : State → Option Bytes → OracleComp PrimBaseSpec Bool /-- Primitive-oracle budget per stage. -/ q_prim : Nat

def AeadIndCpaAdv.BoundedL57–60 ↗#

Query-budget compliance: choose and dist each make at most A.q_prim primitive queries.

def AeadIndCpaAdv.Bounded (A : AeadIndCpaAdv) : Prop := OracleComp.IsQueryBoundP A.choose (fun q => isPrimQuery₀ q = true) A.q_prim ∧ (∀ st c, OracleComp.IsQueryBoundP (A.dist st c) (fun q => isPrimQuery₀ q = true) A.q_prim)

def aeadIndCpaExpL62–71 ↗#

One-time left-or-right IND-CPA experiment under uniform 80-byte MessageKeys; returns a uniform coin if m0.length ≠ m1.length.

noncomputable def aeadIndCpaExp (P : Primitives) (A : AeadIndCpaAdv) : ProbComp Bool := do let b ← $ᵗ Bool let mk ← sampleMessageKeys80 let (ad, m0, m1, st) ← simulateQ (primBaseImpl P) A.choose if m0.length != m1.length then do let coin ← $ᵗ Bool; return coin let ct := P.aeadEnc mk ad (if b then m1 else m0) let b' ← simulateQ (primBaseImpl P) (A.dist st (some ct)) return (b' == b)

def AeadIndCpaL73–75 ↗#

One-time left-or-right IND-CPA advantage against the first-message AEAD.

noncomputable def AeadIndCpa (P : Primitives) (A : AeadIndCpaAdv) : ℝ≥0∞ := 𝒟[aeadIndCpaExp P A].boolBias

def PrfHmacAdv.Bounded (A : PrfHmacAdv) : Prop := OracleComp.IsQueryBoundP A.run (fun q => q.isRight = true) A.q_prf ∧ OracleComp.IsQueryBoundP A.run (fun q => isPrimQuery q = true) A.q_prim

def prfHmacExpL98–117 ↗#

Real-or-random PRF experiment for hmacSha256Ref P k · under a uniform 32-byte key k versus a lazy random function with 32-byte outputs.

noncomputable def prfHmacExp (P : Primitives) (A : PrfHmacAdv) : ProbComp Bool := do let b ← $ᵗ Bool let k ← sampleBytes32 let impl : QueryImpl prfHmacSpec (StateT (List (Bytes × Bytes)) ProbComp) := fun (.eval msg) => do if b then return hmacSha256Ref P k msg else let cache ← get match cache.find? (fun (m, _) => m == msg) with | some (_, t) => return t | none => let t ← liftM sampleBytes32 set ((msg, t) :: cache) return t let fullImpl := (primBaseImpl P).liftTarget (StateT (List (Bytes × Bytes)) ProbComp) + impl let (b', _) ← (simulateQ fullImpl A.run).run [] return (b' == b)

Message-key PRF (PrfMsgKeys)

def effectiveHkdfSaltBytesL157–160 ↗#

Effective 32-byte HKDF salt of an optional SPQR salt (none ↦ 0^32, some s ↦ s zero-padded to 32 bytes; RFC 2104 §2, RFC 5869 §2.2). For s.length ≤ 32, deriveMsgKeysRef at s? agrees with deriveMsgKeysRef at some (effectiveHkdfSaltBytes s?).toList.

def effectiveHkdfSaltBytes (salt? : Option Bytes) : List.Vector UInt8 32 := CryptoGames.effectiveHkdfSalt salt?

inductive PrfMsgKeysQueryL162–168 ↗#

Evaluation query deriveMsgKeys(mkSeed, some salt) at a 32-byte effective salt (DEV-LS25). Indexing by {0,1}^256 avoids collisions between equivalent raw salts (none, some [], some 0^32) and matches the dual-PRF assumption on HMAC in its message slot (Bellare, Bernstein, Gajland, Saha, BBGS'23, Theorem 11).

inductive PrfMsgKeysQuery where | derive (salt : List.Vector UInt8 32) deriving DecidableEq

def prfMsgKeysExpL183–204 ↗#

Real-or-random PRF experiment for deriveMsgKeys mkSeed (some ·) under a uniform 32-byte mkSeed versus a lazy random function into uniform 80-byte MessageKeys.

noncomputable def prfMsgKeysExp (P : Primitives) (A : PrfMsgKeysAdv) : ProbComp Bool := do let b ← $ᵗ Bool let mkSeed ← sampleBytes32 let impl : QueryImpl prfMsgKeysSpec (StateT (List (List.Vector UInt8 32 × MessageKeys)) ProbComp) := fun (.derive salt) => do if b then return P.deriveMsgKeys mkSeed (some salt.toList) else let cache ← get match cache.find? (fun (s, _) => s == salt) with | some (_, out) => return out | none => let out ← liftM sampleMessageKeys80 set ((salt, out) :: cache) return out let fullImpl := (primBaseImpl P).liftTarget (StateT (List (List.Vector UInt8 32 × MessageKeys)) ProbComp) + impl let (b', _) ← (simulateQ fullImpl A.run).run [] return (b' == b)

def PrfMsgKeysL206–208 ↗#

PRF advantage against deriveMsgKeys(mkSeed, ·) over 32-byte effective salts.

noncomputable def PrfMsgKeys (P : Primitives) (A : PrfMsgKeysAdv) : ℝ≥0∞ := 𝒟[prfMsgKeysExp P A].boolBias

First root-KDF oracle

def evalRootKdfOrRoL212–225 ↗#

Evaluates the first rootCreateChain(rk, dh) step of a session either concretely (useRo = false) or via a lazy caching random oracle (useRo = true).

def evalRootKdfOrRo (useRo : Bool) (P : Primitives) (rootRoCache : List ((Bytes × Bytes) × (Bytes × Bytes))) (rk dh : Bytes) : ProbComp ((Bytes × Bytes) × List ((Bytes × Bytes) × (Bytes × Bytes))) := do if !useRo then return (P.rootCreateChain rk dh, rootRoCache) else match rootRoCache.find? (fun (inp, _) => inp == (rk, dh)) with | some (_, out) => return (out, rootRoCache) | none => let rk1 ← sampleBytes32 let ck1 ← sampleBytes32 return ((rk1, ck1), ((rk, dh), (rk1, ck1)) :: rootRoCache)

First-message authentication and privacy game

structure SentOPKEvent where a0 : Bytes -- Sender identity public key b0 : Bytes -- Peer identity public key sb : Bytes -- Peer signed EC pre-key ob : Bytes -- Peer one-time EC pre-key a1 : Bytes -- Sender ephemeral public key pk1 : Bytes -- Peer Kyber-1024 pre-key ct : Bytes -- Kyber-1024 ciphertext m : Bytes -- Encrypted plaintext matched : Bool -- Consumed by a matching `RecvdOPKEvent` deriving DecidableEq, Repr

Recorded honest no-OPK receive event.

structure RecvdNoOPKEvent where bCorr : Bool a0 : Bytes b0 : Bytes sb : Bytes a1 : Bytes pk1 : Bytes ct : Bytes m : Bytes deriving DecidableEq, Repr

def matchSentOPKL279–292 ↗#

Correspondence predicate between a RecvdOPKEvent and an unconsumed SentOPKEvent: compares EC keys up to cofactor (pow8), requires exact sb equality unless the receiver is corrupted (bCorr), and compares fixed-length pk1, ct, and m by byte equality.

def matchSentOPK (P : Primitives) (r : RecvdOPKEvent) (s : SentOPKEvent) : Bool := !s.matched && P.pow8 r.a0 == P.pow8 s.a0 && P.pow8 r.b0 == P.pow8 s.b0 && P.pow8 r.ob == P.pow8 s.ob && P.pow8 r.a1 == P.pow8 s.a1 && P.pow8 r.sb == P.pow8 s.sb && (r.bCorr || r.sb == s.sb) && r.pk1 == s.pk1 && r.ct == s.ct && r.m == s.m

def matchSentNoOPKL294–305 ↗#

No-OPK counterpart of matchSentOPK (injective via (pqspkId, spkId, ekAPk) replay deduplication on receive).

def matchSentNoOPK (P : Primitives) (r : RecvdNoOPKEvent) (s : SentNoOPKEvent) : Bool := !s.matched && P.pow8 r.a0 == P.pow8 s.a0 && P.pow8 r.b0 == P.pow8 s.b0 && P.pow8 r.a1 == P.pow8 s.a1 && P.pow8 r.sb == P.pow8 s.sb && (r.bCorr || r.sb == s.sb) && r.pk1 == s.pk1 && r.ct == s.ct && r.m == s.m

structure AuthInitiatorEntry (S : Setup) where sid : SessionId S peerIkPk : Bytes peerSpkPk : Bytes peerOpkPk? : Option Bytes peerPqspkPk : Bytes spkHonest : Bool opkHonest : Bool pqspkHonest : Bool ekASk : Bytes ephASk : Bytes fresh : Bool challenged : Bool deriving DecidableEq, Repr

def authInitCorruptionClauseL323–334 ↗#

Post-game confidentiality freshness for a challenged initiator session: the peer was an uncorrupted honest principal at send time (s.fresh), and at game end either useRo = true and the peer identity key remains uncorrupted or one of (spk, opk, pqspk) was honestly generated, or useRo = false and pqspk was honestly generated.

def authInitCorruptionClause {S : Setup} (P : Primitives) (useRo : Bool) (principals : List (Nat × PrincipalEntry)) (s : AuthInitiatorEntry S) : Bool := s.fresh && (if useRo then (isHonestUncorruptedPeer P principals s.peerIkPk).isSome || s.spkHonest || s.opkHonest || s.pqspkHonest else s.pqspkHonest)

inductive AuthQueryL336–353 ↗#

Adversary oracle queries in the Auth game: principal and pre-key management, left-or-right sends (sendOPK, sendNoOPK), responder receives (recvOPK, recvNoOPK), random-oracle queries (roQuery, roRootQuery), HNDL secret reveal (revealDhSecrets), and KOSK key registration (registerKey, DEV-PQ15).

def runAuthSendL417–523 ↗#

Executes an honest initiator first-message send (sendOPK or sendNoOPK). Encrypts m_secb when the peer is an uncorrupted honest principal (isFreshPeer) and m0 otherwise; leaks session keys only when the peer identity key is adversarial.

def runAuthSend (useRo : Bool) (S : Setup) (P : Primitives) (sid : SessionId S) (u : Fin S.N_id) (bundle : PreKeyBundleInput) (m0 m1 : Bytes) : StateT (AuthState S) ProbComp AuthResponse := do let st ← get if m0.length != m1.length then return .noneResp if st.usedSendSessions.contains sid then return .noneResp let some (_, uEntry) := st.principals.find? (fun (idx, _) => idx == u.val) | return .noneResp let peerPrincipal? := findHonestPrincipal P st.principals bundle.ikB let isFreshPeer : Bool := match peerPrincipal? with | some (_, pEntry) => !pEntry.corrupted | none => false if !isFreshPeer && m0 != m1 then return .noneResp let msgPlain := if isFreshPeer then (if st.secb then m1 else m0) else m0 if !koskBundleOk P st.principals st.spkBundles st.opkEntries st.advKeys bundle then return .noneResp let ekASk ← liftM sampleScalar32 let kemCoins ← liftM sampleCoins32 let ephASk ← liftM sampleScalar32 let spqrCoins ← liftM sampleCoins32 let sigPkB := resolveSigPk P st.principals bundle.ikB if !(P.sigVerify sigPkB (encodeEC bundle.spkB) bundle.spkSig && P.sigVerify sigPkB (encodeKEM bundle.pqspkB) bundle.pqspkSig) then return .noneResp let some (ss, kemCt) := P.kemEncaps bundle.pqspkB kemCoins | return .noneResp let ekAPk := P.x25519Base ekASk let dh1 := P.x25519 uEntry.secIKA0 bundle.spkB let dh2 := P.x25519 ekASk bundle.ikB let dh3 := P.x25519 ekASk bundle.spkB let dh4? := bundle.opkB?.map (fun (_, opkPk) => P.x25519 ekASk opkPk) let secrets := buildSecrets dh1 dh2 dh3 dh4? ss let (drKey, roCache') ← liftM (evalHkdfOrRo useRo P st.roCache secrets) -- Five-step first-message key schedule. let ephAPk := P.x25519Base ephASk let dhRatchet := P.x25519 ephASk bundle.spkB let ((rk1, ck1_0), rootRoCache') ← liftM (evalRootKdfOrRo useRo P st.rootRoCache drKey.rootKey dhRatchet) let mkSeed := P.chainKdfSeed ck1_0 let ck1_1 := P.chainKdfNext ck1_0 let some (_pqrStA, spqrSalt?, pqRatchetMsg) := P.spqrInitSend drKey.pqrKey spqrCoins | return .noneResp let deriveMessageKeys := P.deriveMsgKeys mkSeed spqrSalt? let ad := firstMsgAD uEntry.ikAPk bundle.ikB ephAPk pqRatchetMsg let aeadCt := P.aeadEnc deriveMessageKeys ad msgPlain let hdr : HandshakeHdr := { ikAPk := uEntry.ikAPk ekAPk := ekAPk spkId := bundle.spkId opkId? := bundle.opkB?.map Prod.fst pqspkId := bundle.pqspkId kemCt := kemCt } let wireMsg : PreKeyMsg := { hdr := hdr ephAPk := ephAPk pqRatchetMsg := pqRatchetMsg aeadCt := aeadCt } let (spkHon, opkHon, pqspkHon) := checkBundleProvenance P st.principals st.spkBundles st.opkEntries bundle let sessEntry : AuthInitiatorEntry S := { sid := sid peerIkPk := bundle.ikB peerSpkPk := bundle.spkB peerOpkPk? := bundle.opkB?.map Prod.snd peerPqspkPk := bundle.pqspkB spkHonest := spkHon opkHonest := opkHon pqspkHonest := pqspkHon ekASk := ekASk ephASk := ephASk fresh := isFreshPeer challenged := isFreshPeer && (m0 != m1) } -- Record send event whenever the peer is an honest principal (corrupted or uncorrupted). let (sentOPK', sentNoOPK') := match peerPrincipal?, bundle.opkB? def pqxdhAuthExpCoreL801–819 ↗#

Core two-key Auth experiment (DEV-PQ13): wins outright if checkAuth ∧ finalSt.hasWonAuth, returns a uniform coin if any challenged session fails authInitCorruptionClause, and otherwise checks b' == secb.

noncomputable def pqxdhAuthExpCore (useRo checkAuth : Bool) (S : Setup) (P : Primitives) (A : AuthAdversary S) : ProbComp Bool := do let secb ← $ᵗ Bool let initSt := AuthState.empty S secb let impl := (QueryImpl.ofLift unifSpec ProbComp).liftTarget (StateT (AuthState S) ProbComp) + pqxdhAuthImpl useRo checkAuth S P let (b', finalSt) ← (simulateQ impl A.run).run initSt let allChallengedClean := finalSt.sessions.all (fun s => !s.challenged || authInitCorruptionClause P useRo finalSt.principals s) if checkAuth && finalSt.hasWonAuth then return true else if !allChallengedClean then let coin ← $ᵗ Bool return coin else return (b' == secb)

def pqxdhAuthExpL821–824 ↗#

Two-key Auth experiment (useRo = true, checkAuth = true).

noncomputable def pqxdhAuthExp (S : Setup) (P : Primitives) (A : AuthAdversary S) : ProbComp Bool := pqxdhAuthExpCore true true S P A

def AuthAdvantageL826–828 ↗#

Advantage |2 Pr[win] - 1| (boolBias) of A in pqxdhAuthExp.

noncomputable def AuthAdvantage (S : Setup) (P : Primitives) (A : AuthAdversary S) : ℝ≥0∞ := 𝒟[pqxdhAuthExp S P A].boolBias

instanceL883–895 ↗#

Query-budget compliance for AuthAdversary S: bounds HkdfRO (b.q_ro), RootKdfRO (b.q_roRoot), initiator (S.N_send_tot), responder (S.N_recv_tot), total game (b.q_total), and online non-RO (b.q_on, isAuthOnlineQuery) queries. Every online query is a game query, so any adversary bounded at b.q_total satisfies q_on at { b with q_on := b.q_total }, and pqxdhAuthAdvantageBoundδ does not depend on q_on.

instance {S : Setup} : HasQueryBound (AuthAdversary S) where QueryBounded A b := OracleComp.IsQueryBoundP A.run isAuthRoQuery b.q_ro ∧ OracleComp.IsQueryBoundP A.run isAuthSendQuery S.N_send_tot ∧ OracleComp.IsQueryBoundP A.run isAuthRecvQuery S.N_recv_tot ∧ OracleComp.IsQueryBoundP A.run isAuthRoRootQuery b.q_roRoot ∧ OracleComp.IsQueryBoundP A.run (fun q => isGameQuery q = true) b.q_total ∧ OracleComp.IsQueryBoundP A.run isAuthOnlineQuery b.q_on

Closed-form advantage bound

def rootKdfRoTermL899–903 ↗#

Statistical boolBias term for the first-step root-KDF random oracle across S.N_sess_tot sessions and q_roRoot adversary .roRootQuery calls: bounds root-key guesses and session input collisions over 32-byte root keys.

noncomputable def rootKdfRoTerm (S : Setup) (q_roRoot : ℕ) : ℝ≥0∞ := 2 * (S.N_sess_tot : ℝ≥0∞) * ((q_roRoot : ℝ≥0∞) + (S.N_sess_tot : ℝ≥0∞)) / (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ^ 256

def pqxdhAuthBoundL905–923 ↗#

Closed-form boolBias advantage bound for Auth, which extends pqxdhKeyIndBound with:

  • 2 · N_send_tot · N_recv_tot / 2^250 for cofactor-8 X25519 collisions between fresh initiator ephemeral keys and prior responder receives;

  • rootKdfRoTerm S q_roRoot for the first root-KDF random-oracle step;

  • 2 · N_sess_tot · (epsPrfCk + epsPrfMsgKeys) for the chain-key and message-key PRF steps;

  • 2 · N_send_tot · epsAeadCpa for left-or-right payload privacy on fresh sends; and

  • 2 · (2 · N_sess_tot · epsPrfHmac + N_recv_tot / 2^64) for 8-byte HMAC tag forgery across at most N_recv_tot receives.

noncomputable def pqxdhAuthBound (S : Setup) (q_roRoot : ℕ) (epsSig epsKemShCr epsGapDh epsPrfCk epsPrfMsgKeys epsAeadCpa epsPrfHmac : ℝ≥0∞) : ℝ≥0∞ := pqxdhKeyIndBound S epsSig epsKemShCr epsGapDh + 2 * (S.N_send_tot : ℝ≥0∞) * (S.N_recv_tot : ℝ≥0∞) / (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ^ 250 + rootKdfRoTerm S q_roRoot + 2 * (S.N_sess_tot : ℝ≥0∞) * epsPrfCk + 2 * (S.N_sess_tot : ℝ≥0∞) * epsPrfMsgKeys + 2 * (S.N_send_tot : ℝ≥0∞) * epsAeadCpa + 2 * (2 * (S.N_sess_tot : ℝ≥0∞) * epsPrfHmac + (S.N_recv_tot : ℝ≥0∞) / (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ^ 64)

One-key Auth game

def pqxdhAuthExpCoreWithL927–945 ↗#

Runs the Auth experiment of pqxdhAuthExpCore against an arbitrary authSpec S implementation impl.

noncomputable def pqxdhAuthExpCoreWith (useRo checkAuth : Bool) (S : Setup) (P : Primitives) (impl : QueryImpl (authSpec S) (StateT (AuthState S) ProbComp)) (A : AuthAdversary S) : ProbComp Bool := do let secb ← $ᵗ Bool let initSt := AuthState.empty S secb let impl' := (QueryImpl.ofLift unifSpec ProbComp).liftTarget (StateT (AuthState S) ProbComp) + impl let (b', finalSt) ← (simulateQ impl' A.run).run initSt let allChallengedClean := finalSt.sessions.all (fun s => !s.challenged || authInitCorruptionClause P useRo finalSt.principals s) if checkAuth && finalSt.hasWonAuth then return true else if !allChallengedClean then let coin ← $ᵗ Bool return coin else return (b' == secb)

theorem pqxdhAuthExpCore_eq_withL947–951 ↗#

theorem pqxdhAuthExpCore_eq_with (useRo checkAuth : Bool) (S : Setup) (P : Primitives) (A : AuthAdversary S) : pqxdhAuthExpCore useRo checkAuth S P A = pqxdhAuthExpCoreWith useRo checkAuth S P (pqxdhAuthImpl useRo checkAuth S P) A := ⋯

def pqxdhAuthImpl1KeyL953–974 ↗#

One-key Auth oracle (DEV-C5): .initPrin u samples a single Curve25519 scalar secIKA0 for both X25519 and XEdDSA (secIKAsign := secIKA0, ikSignPk := ikAPk = P.x25519Base secIKA0), and delegates all other queries to pqxdhAuthImpl true true S P.

def pqxdhAuthImpl1Key (S : Setup) (P : Primitives) : QueryImpl (authSpec S) (StateT (AuthState S) ProbComp) := fun q => match q with | .initPrin u => do let st ← get if st.principals.any (fun (idx, _) => idx == u.val) then return .noneResp let secIKA0 ← liftM sampleScalar32 let ikAPk := P.x25519Base secIKA0 let entry : PrincipalEntry := { secIKA0 := secIKA0 ikAPk := ikAPk secIKAsign := secIKA0 ikSignPk := ikAPk corrupted := false } set { st with principals := (u.val, entry) :: st.principals } return .initPrinResp ikAPk ikAPk | q => pqxdhAuthImpl true true S P q

def pqxdhAuth1KeyExpL976–979 ↗#

One-key Auth experiment (pqxdhAuthExpCoreWith true true on pqxdhAuthImpl1Key).

noncomputable def pqxdhAuth1KeyExp (S : Setup) (P : Primitives) (A : AuthAdversary S) : ProbComp Bool := pqxdhAuthExpCoreWith true true S P (pqxdhAuthImpl1Key S P) A

def Auth1KeyAdvantageL981–986 ↗#

Advantage |2 Pr[win] - 1| (boolBias) of A in pqxdhAuth1KeyExp.

noncomputable def Auth1KeyAdvantage (S : Setup) (P : Primitives) (A : AuthAdversary S) : ℝ≥0∞ := 𝒟[pqxdhAuth1KeyExp S P A].boolBias
